external_entities.name: colleagues
external_entities.description: People who sign in through the identity broker and use applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.
external_entities.notes: Their authentication factors are not described.

external_entities.name: franchise colleagues
external_entities.description: Colleagues from franchise stores who sign in through their own identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The provider's permitted population is not documented.

external_entities.name: franchise stores
external_entities.description: Franchise stores whose colleagues are allowed to sign in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

external_entities.name: franchise identity provider
external_entities.description: An identity provider operated by the franchise side that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not identify the provider or state which colleagues it may vouch for.

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies group-membership changes and leaver changes to the broker overnight.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, accepts franchise identity assertions, and synchronizes directory changes.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The broker signs tokens with a shared signing key and writes sign-ins to an audit log.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application that uses token groups to authorize price changes and transaction voids across stores.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications.
processes.notes: It does not check which store the colleague belongs to.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the broker's token-signing key.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The broker's directory of colleagues and their group memberships.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: Colleagues submit a sign-in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are, including their own devices at home.

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token containing a staff ID and group list to a colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and a list of the groups they are in.

data_flows.name: administer stores
data_flows.description: A colleague presents the token and uses the console to change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.data_description: Token and store administration actions involving prices and transactions.

data_flows.name: fetch public key
data_flows.description: The store admin console fetches the broker's public signing key to verify token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: The public half of the token-signing key.

data_flows.name: read signing key
data_flows.description: The broker accesses its signing key in the key store to sign tokens.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.
data_flows.notes: The same key signs tokens for every application.

data_flows.name: update directory
data_flows.description: The broker maintains colleague and group membership data in the directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: send changes
data_flows.description: The HR system supplies overnight group-membership and leaver changes to the broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.notes: The text also says the broker pulls the changes once a night.
data_flows.data_description: Overnight changes to group membership and colleague status.

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for a franchise colleague and the broker accepts that as a sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the provider is allowed to vouch for.

data_flows.name: write audit log
data_flows.description: The broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_flows.notes: The text does not say what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network where the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: franchise
trust_boundaries.description: The zone controlled by the franchise side, including franchise colleagues, stores, and their identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The identity broker handles confidential data because it processes tokens containing staff IDs and group memberships and accesses a signing key.
assumptions.basis: The broker issues tokens carrying staff IDs and group lists and signs them with a signing key.

assumptions.assumption: The store admin console handles confidential data because it processes authentication tokens and permits changes to prices and transactions.
assumptions.basis: The console uses a token with the store-manager group to change prices and void transactions.

assumptions.assumption: The token issued to a colleague is confidential because it contains a staff ID and group memberships and acts as an authorization credential.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the token carries the colleague's staff ID and group list and is used by applications to decide what the holder may do.

assumptions.assumption: The store administration flow is confidential because it carries an authorization token and involves prices and transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the token authorizes changing prices and voiding transactions.

assumptions.assumption: The key store is confidential because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker keeps its signing key in the key store.

assumptions.assumption: The directory is confidential because it holds colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The public-key retrieval flow is confidential because it carries cryptographic key material, even though the source describes it as the public half.
assumptions.basis: The source states that applications fetch the public half of the signing key from the broker.

assumptions.assumption: The signing-key access flow is confidential because it carries the broker's signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store contains the signing key used by the broker.

assumptions.assumption: The directory update flow is confidential because it carries colleague and group-membership data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory stores colleagues and their groups.

assumptions.assumption: The HR synchronization flow is confidential because it carries colleague status and group-membership changes.
assumptions.basis: The source states that group membership and leaver changes come from the HR system.

assumptions.assumption: The franchise sign-in flow is confidential because it carries an identity-provider assertion about a franchise colleague.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the franchise identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues as a sign-in.
